title: House vs Shell — Boundary Permeability, Exit Cost, Modularity and Interface Quality
status: archive-generated open-systems/network model built from canonical House/Shell distinction
abstract: The project distinguishes House from Shell not by whether a boundary exists but by what the boundary enables. Both protect an interior from an exterior; the scientific difference must therefore be expressed through permeability, selectivity, transparency, exit cost, modularity, autonomy and viability. This paper models House/Shell as an open system partitioned into internal, boundary and external states. A healthy House can reduce harmful coupling while preserving controlled exchange and genuine exits; an unhealthy Shell can preserve internal order while making exit prohibitively costly, routing all exchange through a controlling bottleneck or preventing peripheral capability from surviving outside. Graph conductance and Markov-blanket ideas supply technical neighbors, but neither determines ethical quality by itself. The central conclusion is that boundary quality is multiobjective: low permeability can be protective or imprisoning, high permeability can be enabling or destructive, and only the combination of selective flow, agency, reversibility, capability and outcomes distinguishes the project roles.
epistemic_rule: House, Shell and Qliphoth are project/religious-comparative concepts. Markov blankets, graph cuts, access-control systems and transport/permeability equations are scientific/technical models in their own domains. They do not scientifically identify any person, institution or religious image as a literal Shell.

state_partition.X_B: boundary/interface states including Doors, sensors, credentials, membranes or gateways depending domain
state_partition.markov_blanket_neighbor: In probabilistic graphical models a Markov blanket can render internal and external states conditionally independent given boundary/blanket states under the model.
state_partition.formal_statement: X_I conditionally independent of X_E given X_B for a valid Markov-blanket factorization
state_partition.project_use: Boundary is not absence of relation; it can mediate relation through specialized interface states.

variables.J: cross-boundary flux of a defined quantity
variables.P_B: effective permeability/conductance coefficient with domain-specific units

permeability_model.matrix_extension: J_vec=P_matrix Delta_mu_vec for multiple typed channels when a linear approximation is appropriate
permeability_model.selectivity: S_ab=P_a/P_b for two comparable transported quantities under the same domain conventions
permeability_model.project_lesson: A House can be selectively permeable: some flows are encouraged, some restricted. Perfect openness is not required for healthy relation.
permeability_model.warning: Do not use physical membrane units for legal/social boundaries; retain only the structural form unless a domain-specific flux is measurable.

door_capacity.capacity: C_D=sum_k c_k for additive independent gateway capacities under a specified throughput model
door_capacity.access_probability: p_exit(a,c)=P(agent a can discover, satisfy and execute a valid exit in context c)
door_capacity.exit_cost: E_exit(a,c)=time+money+risk+information+social/legal/resource costs represented as a typed vector before optional normalization
door_capacity.repairability: R_D=P(failed/denied transition can be corrected or appealed within declared process)
door_capacity.shell_signature: Low p_exit combined with high E_exit and high continued-dependence after attempted exit is stronger evidence of capture than mere presence of walls.

network_boundary.cut: For node subset S, cut(S,Sbar)=sum_{i in S,j in Sbar} w_ij in an undirected/nonnegative projection when applicable
network_boundary.conductance: Phi(S)=cut(S,Sbar)/min(vol(S),vol(Sbar)) under a common graph-conductance convention
network_boundary.meaning: Low conductance identifies a graph bottleneck/weakly connected module; high conductance means relatively strong cross-boundary connectivity under the chosen weights.
network_boundary.critical_caution: Low conductance is not ethically bad. A secure/private room can be low-conductance by design. High conductance is not automatically good. An exploitative network can transmit value efficiently. Conductance measures structure, not purpose or consent.

room_modularity.house_principle: Many rooms can remain differentiated while sharing infrastructure and controlled passage.
room_modularity.module_state: Room k has internal state x_k, internal coupling W_kk and gateway couplings W_kell.
room_modularity.separation_question: Are within-room functions coherent enough for local identity/capability while cross-room Doors permit needed exchange?
room_modularity.failure_open: If cross-boundary coupling overwhelms all internal differentiation, rooms cease to function as rooms.
room_modularity.failure_closed: If modules cannot exchange resources/information or exit/reconfigure when needed, protection becomes brittle enclosure.
room_modularity.project_link: This mathematically supports House as unity-with-difference rather than undifferentiated oneness.

house_shell_quality_vector.interpretation: First eight are generally desired when relevant; capture and harm are generally undesired, but priorities and definitions depend on domain.
house_shell_quality_vector.pareto_rule: Compare boundary designs as multiobjective alternatives before inventing a single moral score.
house_shell_quality_vector.why: The same boundary setting can improve one goal and worsen another—for example, stronger privacy may reduce some forms of interoperability.

autonomy_and_boundary.center_removal: A_i(c,tau)=Y_i^remove(c,tau)/Y_i^with from the Garden/Farm companion model
autonomy_and_boundary.boundary_extension: Also test Y_i^exit(tau): performance/capability after the node leaves the bounded system through a legitimate Door.
autonomy_and_boundary.portability: P_i=portable capability/resources/data retained after exit / eligible capability/resources/data before exit under a declared accounting
autonomy_and_boundary.house_signature: A protective House can preserve internal safety while allowing members/rooms to carry meaningful capability through legitimate exits.
autonomy_and_boundary.shell_signature: A captive Shell makes the participant's accumulated capability unusable outside or makes exit technically/legal/socially impossible beyond justified safety constraints.

information_boundary.privacy: I(X_private;Y_external) should remain bounded under the chosen threat/privacy model
information_boundary.useful_exchange: I(X_task;Y_external) or task performance should remain sufficient for intended cooperation
information_boundary.tradeoff: Boundary design can seek low leakage of private state while preserving high task-relevant information flow.
information_boundary.project_reflection: This supplies a rigorous version of 'walls plus Doors': protect what should remain private while enabling what must cross.

boundary_control.constraints: x(t) in V_safe; gateway actions u constrained by authorization/resource policies
boundary_control.least_privilege_neighbor: Grant only capabilities required for the task rather than universal access.
boundary_control.door_relation: Door logic belongs at the boundary where access conditions change admissible state transitions.
boundary_control.project_rule: Healthy protection should be explainable in terms of explicit threats, functions and constraints rather than arbitrary dependence on a gatekeeper.

house_to_shell_transition.transition_hypothesis: A House can drift toward Shell when exit/appeal become less feasible, capabilities become less portable, and boundary control increasingly serves center preservation rather than declared protection/function.
house_to_shell_transition.not_single_threshold: No universal numerical Shell threshold is claimed; domain-specific norms and constraints are required.
house_to_shell_transition.door_failure_connection: False Door, infinite deepening and credential capture are observable failure modes already present in the canonical Door atlas.

empirical_examples.software_platform: measure API/export capability, data portability, account-exit friction, moderation transparency, dependency on proprietary interfaces
empirical_examples.organization: measure internal modularity, cross-team throughput, ability to transfer skills, exit costs and appeal mechanisms
empirical_examples.secure_system: measure authorized throughput, unauthorized leakage, false reject/accept rates and recovery/appeal paths
empirical_examples.archive: measure source access, navigation between rooms/topics, export/reuse, broken links, provenance portability and whether reader conclusions survive outside one UI

measurement_protocol.declare: system boundary, internal/external states, legitimate protected assets, permitted flow types, agent classes, Doors, threat model and time horizon
measurement_protocol.falsifier: If a supposedly House-like design does not improve protection or viable differentiated function and instead primarily increases opaque dependency/exit cost without compensating safety benefit, the House interpretation is weakened in that empirical domain.

conclusions: House and Shell cannot be distinguished by closedness alone; both are boundary systems.
The scientifically informative variables are selective permeability, exit/appeal, portability, modularity, privacy, capability and objective.
A healthy Door is neither unrestricted openness nor arbitrary gatekeeping; it is a typed interface with explicit conditions and repair paths.
Unity-with-difference has a concrete systems meaning: modules can preserve local structure while exchanging selected resources/information through boundaries.
Boundary science improves the project by making 'capture' a measurable failure hypothesis rather than a label inferred from disagreement.
